subject: Brightleaf POC: SLO fitment follow-up (p95/p99, streaming, concurrency)
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wu <sam.wu@brightleaf.ai>, Anna Cho <anna.cho@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Brightleaf POC: SLO fitment follow-up (p95/p99, streaming, concurrency)

Hi Sam / Anna — thanks again for a productive demo earlier. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can scope the POC and latency qualification run: 

Summary of what we heard from Brightleaf during the call:
- Primary API pattern: short chat turns (avg prompt+response ~ 6 tokens prompt / ~60 tokens response), but we also have a streaming use case for real-time transcription snippets that are held open ~4–8s on average.
- Concurrency: steady-state 40–60 concurrent active sessions during business hours; peak bursts up to ~150 concurrent sessions for short windows.
- Target SLOs you care about (to confirm): p95 end-to-end <= 180 ms, p99 <= 450 ms for the standard non-streaming endpoint. Streaming tail latency objective: median chunk-to-chunk <= 60 ms.
- Throughput: typical sustained 220 QPS overall with 30% of requests using streaming.

Immediate asks / clarifications we need from Brightleaf to finalize the POC runbook: 
1) Please confirm the p95/p99 targets above or provide updated values (you mentioned 150/400 in the call — want the canonical target).
2) Share a 48-72 hour traffic sample (anonymized) or the CSV traffic profile you referenced so our infra team can synthesize realistic arrival patterns.
3) Any payload-size constraints (max prompt length / response size) and whether you expect frequent long-form responses (>800 tokens).
4) A target test window (dates/times) and whether we can run synthetic load from our hosted region (us-west) or you prefer cross-region testing.

What Redwood will provide for the POC:
- A reproducible runbook: test harness, traffic shaping script, and exact curl/postman examples.
- Two candidate endpoints: (1) hosted-optimised model configuration tuned for low tail latency, (2) fallback model variant for graceful degradation.
- Per-request traces (x-request-id) and p95/p99 breakdown by hop.

Proposed next steps (if you confirm):
- Sam/Anna: send traffic profile CSV and confirm final SLOs by EOD Thu 2027-04-08.
- Redwood (Karthik & Marissa): produce runbook and schedule a 2-hour test window next week (we propose Tue 2027-04-13 09:00–11:00 PT).
- Post-test: 48-hour analysis and a short write-up showing token cost delta and tail-latency breakdown.

Attachments: I attached a sample SLO matrix template to fill in (slo-matrix-brightleaf.xlsx) and a placeholder for traffic profile (brightleaf_traffic_profile.csv).

Thanks — looking forward to the run.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Sam Wu <sam.wu@brightleaf.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anna Cho <anna.cho@brightleaf.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightleaf POC: SLO fitment follow-up (p95/p99, streaming, concurrency)

Thanks Lauren — great recap. A few clarifications and I attached the traffic CSV you requested.

Confirmed SLOs: our internal product asks are p95 <= 150 ms, p99 <= 500 ms for the standard endpoint. For streaming, our requirement is chunk-latency median <= 80 ms; we can tolerate higher p99s for streaming but want predictable chunk cadence.

Traffic profile: attached brightleaf_traffic_profile.csv (48-hour sample, anonymized). Key notes:
- Avg request payload ~ 350 bytes; 95th percentile payload ~ 1.2KB.
- Streaming sessions are ~32% of total requests over the sample window.
- Peak concurrency observed in sample: 138 active sessions.

Test window: Tue 2027-04-13 10:00–12:00 PT works for us. We are okay with Redwood running the synthetic load from us-west.

One ask: during the test we will want to validate per-region routing — can you include a short run from us-east as a sanity check? If not, we can skip for the first run.

Sam
Sam Wu
Head of Integrations, Brightleaf Health
sam.wu@brightleaf.ai

Attachment: brightleaf_traffic_profile.csv

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wu <sam.wu@brightleaf.ai>, Anna Cho <anna.cho@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightleaf POC: SLO fitment follow-up (p95/p99, streaming, concurrency)

Hi Sam / Anna — thanks for the traffic file and the SLO confirmation. A few technical clarifications from our infra side before we finalize the runbook: 

1) Traffic synthesis: your CSV looks good. We'll replay arrival patterns and payload-size distribution. We will tag every request with x-request-id and return a small JSON with timing metadata.
2) Streaming harness: for streaming sessions we need to simulate the real client keep-alive pattern (open socket, send partial prompts, close after final chunk). Please confirm if your clients use server-sent events or WebSocket; the CSV has a column "stream_type" but it's not populated.
3) Route and fallback policy: for p99 protection we'll run a canary with a more quantized/latency-optimized model (lower precision) and measure quality delta. Please confirm whether you're comfortable with a fallback that can degrade quality in favor of tail latency for up to 5% of requests during peak bursts.
4) Observability: we will provide traces and per-token cost estimates. To correlate, we need a sample of request IDs from your production logs (even a small subset) or permission to align by timestamp range.
5) Data handling: since the sample contains PHI-ish strings, we'll redact or run entirely in a synthetic dataset derived from the sample unless you provide an NDA/procurement channel for covered test data.

If you confirm stream type and fallback tolerance, we'll finalize the runbook and load scripts today and share a run checklist by end of day.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Technical Lead, Performance Engineering, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Wu <sam.wu@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brightleaf POC: SLO fitment follow-up (p95/p99, streaming, concurrency)

Perfect — thanks Sam and Karthik. Quick confirmations from my side: 
- Brightleaf confirmed SLOs: p95 150 ms, p99 500 ms (standard). Streaming median chunk <= 80 ms.
- Stream transport: Anna confirmed via separate note that Brightleaf uses WebSocket-based streaming for their clients.
- Fallback tolerance: Brightleaf agrees to up to 5% degraded-quality fallback during peak bursts for the purposes of the POC.
- Test window locked: Tue 2027-04-13 10:00–12:00 PT. Redwood will run primary traffic from us-west and a short sanity run from us-east during the second hour.

I will circulate a one-page run checklist and the SLO matrix pre-filled with the confirmed targets. Karthik / Marissa — can you share the runbook and the short playbook for interpreting p99 traces by EOD today?

Thanks all — see you next week.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
